fixes: f-ga-exponents-logarithms variables: 'p, q integers in a fractional exponent (q != 0)' allowed a negative or zero root index, for which the q-th root in a^(p/q) = qth-root(a^p) is undefined; now 'integers in a fractional exponent p/q, with q >= 1 (q is the root index)'.

f-ga-exponents-logarithms meaning: added the missing condition a != 0 for a^(-n) = 1/a^n (stated before only for a^0 = 1), 'with q a positive integer' for the fractional-power rule, and the condition a > 0, a != 1 for the special value log_b(a) * log_a(b) = 1.

f-ga-shape-transformations example: '(4,-2): translating by (-1,3) gives (3,1); rotating 90 deg anticlockwise gives (-1,3); reflecting in the x-axis gives (-1,-3)' did not say that the steps are chained, and rotating the stated point (4,-2) gives (2,4), not (-1,3). It now says the three transformations are applied in turn to the result of the previous step, shows the rule (x,y) -> (-y,x), and notes that rotating (4,-2) directly gives (2,4).

c-ga-english-grammar math (interrupted action) and commonMistakes[0]: taught only the past continuous ('was reading ... when the power went off'), although the official key of DA2025-S5-Q02, the one interrupted-action PYQ in the bank, is the past perfect continuous 'had been playing'. Added that had been + -ing also describes an action in progress up to the moment of interruption, stressing its duration (original example: 'She had been reading for an hour when the power went off'), and added the same alternative to the common mistake.

c-ga-english-grammar gateRelevance: 'fill two or three blanks with a matching sequence of words (often prepositions or articles), or pick the grammatically correct sentence' was unsupported: the bank's grammar MCQs are DA2025-S5-Q02 (one verb blank) and DA2026-S8-Q06 (three preposition blanks), with no article item and no pick-the-correct-sentence item. It now describes those two formats and lists picking the correct sentence as 'another format to prepare for'. intuition: 'Grammar questions in GA are short: ...' -> 'A grammar item can be ...'.

c-ga-reading-narrative-sequencing gateRelevance: 'Narrative sequencing appears as jumbled sentences with candidate orders' was unsupported, because no DA PYQ from 2024-2026 is tagged ga-narrative; it now says sequencing is in the syllabus but has no item in these papers and 'can be set as' jumbled sentences. 'Reading is examined through short passages (a paragraph or two ...) followed by an MCQ: inferred / main idea / assumption / best supported' -> the bank's only reading item (DA2024-S1-Q06) asks what can be inferred; main idea, assumption and best-supported are now listed as 'Other questions to prepare for'. math step 4: 'GA gives candidate orders ...; usually one survives' -> 'when the options list candidate orders ...; if more than one survives, check the remaining links'.

c-ga-logical-numerical-reasoning math: '(assuming, as GA questions do, that every named class has at least one member)' was an unsupported claim about GATE; now '(using the traditional convention that every named class has at least one member; without it, all A are B would not give some B are A)', which also states why the assumption matters. definition: 'The statements in GA logic questions are of a few kinds' -> 'Logic questions are built from a few kinds of statement'. gateRelevance: 'Analytical questions in GA ask' -> 'can ask'.

c-ga-vocabulary-analogies gateRelevance: 'Typical patterns:' -> 'Patterns to prepare for:'. Fill-the-blank vocabulary items and number/figure analogies have no DA PYQ in the bank, so 'typical' was unsupported. definition: 'GA asks for the missing term' -> 'The question asks for the missing term'.

c-ga-mensuration-spatial-reasoning gateRelevance: 'are usually built around a figure. Typical patterns:' -> 'can be built around a figure. Patterns to prepare for:' (no frequency claim is supported by content/exam/pattern.json). intuition: 'Most of these problems' -> 'Many of these problems'.

c-ga-percentages-ratios-data-interpretation gateRelevance: removed the unsupported frequency claim 'The options are often close together' (now 'When the options are close together, ...'); 'DI questions present' -> 'can present'; 'Percentage and ratio questions also appear without a chart' -> 'can also come without a chart'. intuition: the unsupported statistic 'Most DI errors are reading errors' -> 'Many DI errors are reading errors rather than arithmetic errors'.

(for example, with ...)' (the bank has a single instance of the identity, DA2026-S8-Q04). intuition: 'Most exponent questions collapse' -> 'Many exponent questions collapse'.
